adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle key is created with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and only afterward given a TTL via `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These are two separate Redis commands; if the process crashes or is killed after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key will remain without an expiration. Because subsequent calls will see `setnx` fail, `retrieved_recently?` will return true forever for that `embed_url`, permanently preventing retrieval until the key is manually deleted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:64 — absolutize_urls strips all leading slashes, so protocol-relative `//cdn/x.jpg` links are rewritten to the embed host and break

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, both `href` and `src` are rewritten whenever they `start_with?('/')`. This condition matches protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn/x.jpg`. The rewrite uses `href.sub(/^\/+/, '')`, which removes *all* leading slashes, turning `//cdn/x.jpg` into `cdn/x.jpg`, then prefixes it with the embed page host (e.g. `http://example.com/cdn/x.jpg`). That is a functional bug because protocol-relative links are intended to keep their original host (or at least become `scheme://cdn/...`), not be rewritten to the embed host.

The candidate additionally mentions injection risk, but it still covers the same core issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — Host-page origin check uses substring match (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)) instead of exact origin comparison, so unrelated origins can drive the discourse-resize protocol
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue flag the same security flaw: using `indexOf`/substring matching for origin validation allows spoofed or unrelated origins (e.g., `evil-discourseUrl.com`) to pass the check, enabling unauthorized message handling (resize protocol).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:133 — raw_html cook path returns raw and bypasses the Plugin::Filter(:after_post_cook) contract, so every consumer of `cooked` (serializers, RSS, email) receives unfiltered third-party HTML

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which skips both `post_analyzer.cook(*args)` (the normal cooking/sanitization/rendering pipeline) and `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`. The new import path (`TopicEmbed.import` / `PollFeed`) sets `cook_method: :raw_html` for third-party content and `skip_validations: true`, and views render it with `raw post.cooked`, so unfiltered HTML from RSS/Readability will be stored/served as-is and can reach other `cooked` consumers beyond the embed view (serializers/emails/etc.).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:19 — Response depends on Referer (access check + X-Frame-Options) and current_user but is marked cacheable for 1 minute with no Vary, so shared caches can leak the embed HTML across hosts/users

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, the response is explicitly made cacheable via `discourse_expires_in 1.minute`. The rendered HTML depends on request-specific inputs: (1) access is gated by `request.referer` in `ensure_embeddable`, and (2) the body varies by `current_user` because `TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})` can produce different visible posts/content depending on the user/session. There is no `Vary` on `Referer`/cookies/authorization shown, so an intermediary/shared cache that keys only on URL+query could serve cached embed HTML across different users and potentially bypass the referer-based access control by answering from cache without hitting the app. This risk is introduced by marking the response cacheable while it varies on user/referer.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:7 — Embed snippet requires an undocumented trailing slash on discourseUrl and an existing #discourse-comments element, with no normalization or guard for embedders

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js the iframe src is built via string concatenation: `discourseUrl + "embed/best?..."`. If `discourseUrl` does not end with `/` (e.g., `https://forum.example.com`), the resulting URL becomes `https://forum.example.comembed/best?...`, which is invalid. Also, the code does `comments.appendChild(iframe)` immediately after `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` with no null check; if the embedding page lacks that element, this will throw at runtime. Both are concrete, verifiable assumptions/defects present in the diff (no normalization/guard).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:9 — Missing embed_url raises ActionController::ParameterMissing, giving embedders a 500 instead of a 4xx contract response

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, `embed_url = params.require(:embed_url)` will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` when absent. In Rails this exception is typically handled by the framework and results in a 4xx (commonly 400 Bad Request), not an unhandled 500. The included spec (`it "is 404 without an embed_url"`) only asserts `response.should_not be_success` and does not demonstrate a 500 being returned. Nothing in the diff shows custom exception handling that would convert `ParameterMissing` into a 500, so the claim of a 500 is not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:28 — X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL is a non-standard value that some browsers do not honor; the header should be removed for embeddable responses

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"` in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`. `X-Frame-Options` only defines `DENY`, `SAMEORIGIN`, and the obsolete `ALLOW-FROM`; `ALLOWALL` is not a standardized/recognized value. As a result, some browsers may ignore the header or treat it as invalid, which can prevent the embed from working reliably (especially if other middleware/defaults set a restrictive X-Frame-Options). This is a concrete compatibility/correctness issue introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:8 — Height is posted only once on window.onload with no re-post on later content/image layout changes and no host-initiated request, so the iframe keeps a stale height

adjudication.rationale: In app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb the embedded document posts its height to the parent only inside window.onload, via parent.postMessage({type: 'discourse-resize', height: document['body'].offsetHeight}, ...). There is no subsequent postMessage on window resize, DOM mutations, or other layout changes. On the parent side (app/assets/javascripts/embed.js) the iframe height is only updated when receiving these messages. Therefore, if the iframe’s content height changes after initial load (e.g., host page resizes causing reflow, late-loading content, font/layout shifts), the iframe height can become stale because no further resize messages are sent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 — <%- end if %>` is invalid Ruby and makes the template fail to compile, so every successful /embed/best request 500s (verified via ERB compile).

adjudication.rationale: In app/views/embed/best.html.erb the ERB block closes with `<%- end if %>`, which emits Ruby code `end if` with no condition following `if`. Ruby requires a condition for a postfix `if` modifier (e.g., `end if some_condition`), so this is a SyntaxError during ERB compilation/rendering. The line should be just `<%- end %>` (or provide a condition), otherwise the template cannot compile and will 500 when rendered.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:65 — Stripping all leading slashes rewrites protocol-relative URLs (`//cdn.host/x.png`) into `http://embedhost/cdn.host/x.png`, breaking those links/images.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, any `href`/`src` starting with `'/'` is rewritten using `href.sub(/^\/+/, '')` (and similarly for `src`). This condition also matches protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.host/x.png`. For those, the code strips both slashes and prefixes with the embed page origin, producing `#{prefix}/cdn.host/x.png` (e.g., `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.host/x.png`) instead of preserving the protocol-relative `//cdn.host/x.png` (or converting it to `http(s)://cdn.host/x.png`). That breaks protocol-relative asset links.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — i.content` is nil for feeds without content:encoded, so `.scrub` raises NoMethodError and aborts the whole poll (retry: false) instead of skipping the item.
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that `i.content` can be nil for feeds lacking `content:encoded`, causing `.scrub` to raise `NoMethodError` and abort processing. This is the same core issue as the golden comment (unsafe assumption that `i.content` is always present and needs a fallback, e.g., to `description`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:32 — embed.post` can be nil (post deleted/purged while the TopicEmbed row remains), and `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` then raises NoMethodError.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, when an existing TopicEmbed row is found, it does `post = embed.post` and then unconditionally constructs `PostRevisor.new(post)` if the SHA changed. Because the migration adds `post_id` as NOT NULL but does not add a foreign key, and the model has no dependent/constraint guaranteeing the referenced Post still exists, `embed.post` can return nil if the post was deleted/purged while the TopicEmbed row remains. In that case `PostRevisor.new(nil)` will later dereference `@post` (e.g., `@post.acting_user = ...`) and raise a NoMethodError. The diff introduces this risk and contains no guard (e.g., return/delete embed if post missing).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:24 — PostCreator#create returns an unsaved post with errors on failure, so `post.present?` passes and `TopicEmbed.create!` inserts NULL topic_id/post_id, raising a NOT NULL violation instead of skipping.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, it does `post = creator.create` and then guards only with `if post.present?` before calling `TopicEmbed.create!` using `post.topic_id` and `post.id` (both NOT NULL per migration). In Rails, an unsaved `Post` object with validation/creation errors is still `present?`, so this guard does not ensure `post` is persisted. If `PostCreator#create` returns a non-persisted post on failure (a common pattern in service objects like this), `TopicEmbed.create!` will be invoked with nil `topic_id`/`post_id`, causing a NOT NULL violation (or other exception) rather than cleanly skipping. The diff does not show `PostCreator#create`, so the exact behavior can’t be proven from the diff alone, but the risk is directly created by relying on `present?` instead of `persisted?`/`id` checks while inserting into a table with NOT NULL constraints.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:37 — content_sha1 is updated unconditionally even when `revise!` returns false (no revision applied), so the stored hash no longer reflects the post content and the update is never retried.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an existing embed is found and `content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`, it calls `revisor.revise!(...)` and then immediately executes `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` without checking the return value of `revise!` (or otherwise confirming the post was actually updated). Since `PostRevisor#revise!` can return `false` (it early-returns `false` when `should_revise?` fails), this can result in `topic_embeds.content_sha1` being updated even though the post content was not changed, leaving the stored hash inconsistent with the post and preventing future retries because subsequent imports will see matching hashes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — SETNX + EXPIRE are not atomic; a crash between them leaves the throttle key with no TTL, permanently blocking retrieval for that embed_url.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb `retrieved_recently?` uses `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then separately calls `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These two commands are not atomic; if the process crashes or is interrupted after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` is executed, the key will exist without a TTL. Since future calls will see `setnx` fail and return `true` (throttled), retrieval for that `embed_url` can be blocked indefinitely until the key is manually cleared.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:20 — Check-then-insert on embed_url races with concurrent PollFeed/RetrieveTopic runs and violates the unique index on topic_embeds.embed_url.

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. `TopicEmbed.import` does a non-atomic read-then-create:

- It checks `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and if blank later does `TopicEmbed.create!(embed_url: url, ...)`.
- The migration adds `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`.

With concurrent executions (e.g., multiple PollFeed runs, RetrieveTopic jobs, or parallel web requests hitting `EmbedController#best` enqueueing retrieval), two workers can both observe no existing row and then both attempt `create!`, causing one to raise on the unique index (RecordNotUnique). There is no locking/upsert or rescue in this method to make it safe.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — Adding a NOT NULL column with a default to the huge `posts` table forces a full table rewrite under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock (PG < 11), blocking the site during deploy.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a migration `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`. On PostgreSQL versions prior to 11, adding a column with a non-NULL default typically rewrites the entire table and requires an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock for the duration of the operation. Since this targets the `posts` table (commonly large in production), this can block reads/writes during deploy. The migration as written does not use a safer multi-step approach (add nullable column, backfill in batches, add NOT NULL constraint).

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — Editing an already-released migration to add `force: true` is a no-op on existing installs and silently DROPs an existing `top_topics` table (data loss) wherever it does re-run.

db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 — create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` issues an unconditional DROP TABLE IF EXISTS, destroying existing embed rows if the migration is ever re-run.

adjudication.rationale: The migration explicitly uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`, which in Rails will drop the table if it already exists before recreating it. While the table is new in this diff (so the first run is fine), the proposed finding is correct that re-running this migration against an existing `topic_embeds` table would destroy any existing rows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:6 — embed_url` is a plain `t.string` (varchar 255) but stores arbitrary article/feed URLs, which routinely exceed 255 chars and will raise on insert; needs `:text` or a larger limit.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` defines `embed_url` as `t.string` with no explicit limit, which in Rails maps to a 255-character `varchar`. The new code stores full external article/feed URLs directly into `topic_embeds.embed_url` (e.g., from RSS `i.link` / `i.id` and `TopicEmbed.import_remote`), with only a scheme check and no length validation or truncation. On common DBs (notably Postgres and MySQL in strict mode), inserting a URL longer than 255 will raise an error (`value too long`), breaking imports/embedding for long URLs. Using `:text` or a larger limit would avoid this defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:11 — No index on `topic_id`/`post_id` even though TopicEmbed is queried and joined by topic_id (e.g. `TopicEmbed.where(topic_id: ...)`).

adjudication.rationale: The migration creates `topic_embeds` with a unique index on `embed_url` only. In the added application code, `TopicEmbed` lookups are consistently done by `embed_url` (`where(embed_url: ...)`, `topic_id_for_embed` plucks by `embed_url`, and existence checks use `embed_url`). There is no new code in the diff that queries or joins `topic_embeds` by `topic_id`/`post_id` in a way that demonstrably requires indexes for correctness; the only `where(topic_id: ...)` usage appears in a spec assertion. This is a potential performance optimization, not a clear, verifiable defect introduced by the diff, and the proposed finding overstates actual usage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:20 — TopicEmbed.import` checks-then-creates without a uniqueness validation or rescue, so concurrent embed retrievals hit the DB unique index on embed_url and raise RecordNotUnique.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, later does `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)` inside a transaction. The migration adds a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`, but the model does not add `validates_uniqueness_of :embed_url` nor does it rescue `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`. Under concurrent imports for the same URL, both workers can observe `embed.blank?` and then race to `create!`, causing a unique-index violation exception. This is a real correctness/robustness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:131 — Post#cook` reads the new `cook_method` column, so any app instance started before the migration runs will error; column must be deployed ahead of the code.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Post#cook` logic that calls `cook_method` (app/models/post.rb). If the application code is deployed/restarted before that migration has been applied, the `Post` model will not have a `cook_method` attribute method (since ActiveRecord defines attribute methods from the schema at boot), and calling `cook_method` will raise (e.g., `NoMethodError`), breaking post cooking. So there is a real deployment-order/schema-compatibility problem introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb:33 — Already-released migration file edited (trailing newline removed); harmless here but existing installs will never re-run it, so real fixes cannot be delivered this way.

This is at most a process/style concern, not a verifiable defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — contents <<` mutates the caller-owned string argument in place instead of building a new string

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:28 — ensure_embeddable` also mutates response headers (X-Frame-Options), a side effect its name does not convey

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — Calling `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously from a request-triggered job couples the retriever to the whole feed-polling job

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it directly runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously. `PollFeed#poll_feed` performs network I/O (`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`) and imports every item in the feed, so invoking it inline from an on-demand retriever (itself triggered by the `/embed/best` flow via `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`) couples single-URL retrieval to the entire feed-polling process and can make the retriever job unexpectedly heavy/slow and repeatedly poll the feed outside its scheduled cadence.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — Adding `force: true` to an already-shipped migration is unrelated to this PR and silently drops an existing table on re-run

While this migration normally won’t re-run once recorded in `schema_migrations`, changing it this way does introduce a real risk of silent data loss in scenarios where the table exists but the migration is run again (e.g., inconsistent/partially migrated DBs or manual schema changes), whereas without `force: true` Rails would raise an error instead of dropping the table. It’s also unrelated to the embedding changes in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — Disqus importer silently lost its `--category` option and topic `created_at`, an unrelated feature regression bundled into this PR

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — perform_retrieve runs the entire hourly PollFeed job synchronously (full feed download + import of every item) for each embed URL miss, duplicating the scheduled job's work.

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In lib/topic_retriever.rb#perform_retrieve, when an embed URL is missing it does:

```rb
if SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?
  Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})
  return if TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?
end
```

Jobs::PollFeed is a scheduled job (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) intended to run hourly and it performs a full `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` followed by iterating `rss.items.each` and importing each item. Calling it directly here makes the full feed download+import run synchronously as part of each TopicRetriever miss (which is triggered via EmbedController enqueuing Jobs::RetrieveTopic when no TopicEmbed exists). That duplicates the scheduled job’s work and can cause significant unnecessary load/latency when multiple distinct embed URLs are requested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — open() on the feed URL has no timeout, redirect or size limit, so a slow/huge remote feed blocks the worker (and the inline TopicRetriever path) indefinitely.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the feed is fetched with `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` (via `open-uri`) without any explicit `open_timeout`/`read_timeout`, response size limit, or other safeguards. This means a slow/unresponsive server or very large feed can tie up the Sidekiq worker for a long time (and potentially consume lots of memory while parsing). Additionally, `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline, so this unbounded fetch can also block the embed retrieval path, as the finding states.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20 — feed_key computes a cache key that is never used, so there is no conditional GET/If-Modified-Since and the whole feed is refetched and every item re-hashed and re-queried each run.

The polling logic always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates all items on every run, with no use of feed_key to store/compare Last-Modified/ETag or otherwise short-circuit when unchanged. So the key is dead code and the job will refetch and reprocess the full feed each time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — import_remote does open(url).read, materializing the entire remote page in memory with no timeout or size cap before Readability parses it.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import_remote` the code does `open(url).read` and passes the full string into `Readability::Document.new(...)`. This unconditionally materializes the entire remote response in memory and there is no size limit enforced in this method. Also, there is no explicit open/read timeout configuration passed to `open-uri` here, so the request can potentially hang longer than desired depending on defaults/environment. This is a verifiable resource-consumption/DoS risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — A RetrieveTopic job is enqueued on every cache-missing request with no dedupe before enqueue (throttle is only checked inside the job), so a popular embedding page floods Sidekiq with redundant jobs.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil, it unconditionally calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` for that request path. There is no controller-level check (redis key, existing job, etc.) to avoid enqueueing duplicates. The only throttling/dedup behavior shown in the diff is inside `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` (redis `setnx` + expire) and `perform_retrieve` (early return if embed already exists), which runs when the job executes—not when it is enqueued. So repeated cache-miss requests can enqueue many redundant `retrieve_topic` jobs, potentially flooding Sidekiq even if each job later no-ops quickly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:19 — The 1-minute cache directive is also applied to the 'loading' placeholder whose script reloads every 30s, so reloads are served stale from caches and lengthen time-to-content.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is executed unconditionally at the end of the action, regardless of whether it rendered the real embed view or the `'loading'` placeholder (the `else` branch does `render 'loading'`). The loading template (`app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`) triggers `document.location.reload()` every 30 seconds. With a 60-second cache TTL applied to that loading response, a reload within 30 seconds can be satisfied from cache (browser/proxy) instead of hitting the server, delaying the first non-loading response until the cache expires. This is a concrete behavioral mismatch introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:16 — post.user is dereferenced per post in the render loop, risking an N+1 user lookup if TopicView's best-posts query does not eager-load users.

adjudication.rationale: The template iterates `@topic_view.posts` and accesses `post.user` fields, but the diff does not show how `TopicView` loads its posts (whether it `includes(:user)`/preloads users). adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` has no open/read timeout, so a slow or hanging feed host can block a Sidekiq worker indefinitely

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the code does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`, which does not pass explicit timeout options. However, the finding’s claim that this can block a Sidekiq worker “indefinitely” is not verifiable from the diff: Ruby’s open-uri uses Net::HTTP, which has default `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` values (commonly 60s) rather than no timeout at all. While adding explicit timeouts could be a robustness improvement, the “indefinite hang” assertion is overstated and not a clear defect demonstrably introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — open(url).read` in import_remote has no timeout or size limit, so a slow/huge remote page can hang or balloon the RetrieveTopic worker

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/topic_embed.rb#import_remote`, the code does `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)`. This uses `open-uri` to fetch the entire remote response body into memory with no explicit `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` and no limit on bytes read. This method is invoked from background execution paths (`TopicRetriever#fetch_http` and `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`), so a slow server, hanging connection, or extremely large page can tie up the worker and/or consume excessive memory. The diff introduces this behavior and does not implement any safeguards.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 — No per-item rescue in the feed loop: one bad item (nil/invalid content, import failure) aborts the whole poll and skips all remaining items

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the job does `rss.items.each` and inside calls `i.link`, `i.id`, and especially `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` followed by `TopicEmbed.import(...)` with no per-item exception handling. Any exception raised by a single malformed/unsupported feed item (e.g., `i.content` being nil causing `nil.scrub` -> NoMethodError, invalid encoding, or an exception from `TopicEmbed.import`) will abort `poll_feed` immediately and prevent processing the remaining items in that run. This is amplified by `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so the whole poll run is lost until the next scheduled execution.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — Redis throttle uses non-atomic SETNX then EXPIRE; a crash between the two leaves a TTL-less key that permanently blocks retrieval of that embed_url

adjudication.rationale:
Real issue. In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, throttling is implemented as:

- `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")`
- then `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`

These are two separate Redis commands. If the process crashes, is killed, or otherwise fails after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key will be created without a TTL. Because subsequent calls treat any existing key as “retrieved_recently?” (returning true), that embed_url can become permanently throttled until the key is manually deleted. This is a well-known correctness bug with SETNX+EXPIRE split usage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — RetrieveTopic synchronously runs the entire feed poll (`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute`) inline, so concurrent misses each refetch and reimport the whole feed

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/topic_retriever.rb` `perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` directly when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, before falling back to `fetch_http`. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` fetches and parses the entire RSS/Atom feed (`SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`) and iterates all items to import them. This is done inline in the request-triggered retrieval path (via `EmbedController` enqueuing `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`, which runs `TopicRetriever#retrieve`), not as a scheduled/background-only operation. While there is a Redis throttle, it is keyed by `@embed_url` (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so misses for different URLs on the same embeddable host can each trigger a full feed fetch and iteration, making the “refetch and reimport the whole feed per miss” concern verifiable from the diff (even if exact concurrency depends on URLs).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:15 — Check-then-create against the unique embed_url index is racy; concurrent imports raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, which is unrescued and kills the job

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicEmbed.import` does a check-then-create on `embed_url`: it queries `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, later calls `TopicEmbed.create!` (inside a transaction) with that same `embed_url`. The migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` adds `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`, so concurrent callers importing the same URL can both observe `embed.blank?` and then race to insert, causing one to raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`. There is no rescue/retry path in `import` or the calling jobs (`PollFeed`, `RetrieveTopic`), so the exception can bubble up and fail the job run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:32 — embed.post` can be nil (post deleted/purged), so `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` raises NoMethodError and aborts the whole feed poll

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` then `post = embed.post` and unconditionally constructs `PostRevisor.new(post)` if the content hash changed. Since `topic_embeds.post_id` is stored but there is no foreign key or `dependent` behavior shown, a deleted/purged `Post` would make `embed.post` return `nil`. `PostRevisor` then dereferences `@post` (e.g., `@post.acting_user = @user` in `revise!`), which would raise `NoMethodError` and abort the job loop (e.g., feed polling/import).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:12 — sidekiq_options retry: false` means transient feed/network failures are dropped entirely with no retry before the next hourly run

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the job is explicitly configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false`. The job performs network I/O (`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`) and parsing (`SimpleRSS.parse`), which can raise on transient network/feed errors. With retries disabled, a failure will not be retried by Sidekiq and the polling attempt is effectively lost until the next scheduled (hourly) run. This behavior is directly implied by the diff and is a real robustness/correctness concern for feed importing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — RetrieveTopic is enqueued from the request path on every miss with no dedup, and the loading page auto-reloads every 30s, so crawlers/refreshes can flood the queue

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil it unconditionally calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading`. The `loading.html.erb` view includes JS that reloads the iframe every 30 seconds, which will re-hit `embed#best` and enqueue another `:retrieve_topic` job each time until an embed exists. There is no enqueue-side deduplication/locking in the controller (or job enqueue call). Although `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` throttles the *work* via Redis, duplicate jobs can still accumulate in the queue as no-ops, so repeated refreshes/crawlers can generate many queued jobs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:10 — Raising InvalidParameters for a permanently malformed arg causes Sidekiq to retry the poison job repeatedly instead of discarding it

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::RetrieveTopic#execute the code only raises Discourse::InvalidParameters when args[:embed_url] is missing/blank, not when it is “permanently malformed” (a non-URL string still passes and is handled later by TopicRetriever). The only enqueue shown in the diff (EmbedController#best) always supplies embed_url via params.require(:embed_url), so the poison-job scenario is not demonstrated by this change. Also, whether Discourse::InvalidParameters triggers Sidekiq retries or is treated as a non-retriable error cannot be verified from the diff alone (no sidekiq_options or exception handling is shown here).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — Remote RSS/Atom item content is CGI.unescapeHTML'd and stored verbatim as a raw_html post with no sanitization, so feed-supplied <script>/on* attributes become stored XSS in the embed view and the normal topic view

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the feed item body is taken from `i.content` and only passed through `CGI.unescapeHTML(... .scrub)`, then sent to `TopicEmbed.import`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates the post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`, and `Post#cook` explicitly returns `raw` when `cook_method` is `raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (where sanitization would typically occur). The embed view (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb`) renders `raw post.cooked`, and since `cooked == raw` for `raw_html`, any `<script>` tags or dangerous attributes from the feed content would be stored and rendered as-is (stored XSS).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:131 — cook() returns raw unchanged for cook_method raw_html, bypassing the entire sanitization/cook pipeline for imported posts whose HTML comes from untrusted remote pages

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff adds `Post.cook_methods` with a `:raw_html` option and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw` when `cook_method == :raw_html`, explicitly bypassing the normal cooking/rendering pipeline. That `:raw_html` mode is then used for remote/imported content in `TopicEmbed.import` via `PostCreator.new(..., raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents), ..., cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])`. The imported `contents` come from untrusted external sources: RSS (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` then `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) and HTTP readability scraping (`Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` then `doc.content`). Skipping the cooking/sanitization step means any unsafe HTML that makes it into `raw` will be served as-is (and `embed/best.html.erb` renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`), creating a verifiable XSS risk introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — The remote-supplied url is interpolated unescaped into #{url}, so a feed link containing a single quote injects arbitrary attributes/markup (e.g. onmouseover=) into the stored HTML

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends HTML containing `"#{url}"` directly into `contents` (stored as the post `raw` with `cook_method: :raw_html`, meaning it bypasses the normal cooking/sanitization and later is rendered via `raw post.cooked`). The only validation on `url` is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent a malicious URL containing a single quote (or other HTML-breaking characters). A crafted feed/link like `http://example.com/' onmouseover='alert(1)` would break out of the `href` attribute and inject arbitrary attributes/markup into the stored HTML.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19 — post.cooked is emitted with raw in a page served with X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL, rendering unsanitized imported HTML to embedders

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In app/views/embed/best.html.erb the template renders `post.cooked` via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. The diff introduces a new `Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` mode where `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline (`return raw if cook_method == ...`). TopicEmbed.import creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` using externally sourced `contents` (RSS `i.content` / remote readability content) and does not sanitize it beyond URL absolutization. As a result, arbitrary HTML from the feed/remote page can be stored as raw and emitted unescaped in the embed iframe. The embed response explicitly sets `X-Frame-Options = ALLOWALL`, so this unsanitized HTML is indeed delivered in an embeddable page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) uses Kernel#open, so a feed URL beginning with "|" is executed as a shell command, and no scheme validation is performed on the setting

The candidate flags the same unsafe open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) usage and explicitly notes missing scheme/URL validation, which encompasses the SSRF risk, though it also adds the related Kernel#open pipe-to-shell command execution concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — postMessage targetOrigin is built from the attacker-influenced full request.referer URL interpolated into inline JS rather than a validated origin constant
app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — Origin validation uses discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) (substring match) instead of an exact origin comparison and does not verify e.source is the embed iframe

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, postMessageReceived does `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`, which is a substring check rather than an exact origin match. adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:12 — Every example stubs `poll_feed` itself, so the entire new feed body (SimpleRSS parse/open, link-vs-id fallback, CGI.unescapeHTML/scrub, TopicEmbed.import) has zero coverage and no RSS vs Atom shape test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:18 — "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" are tautological: feed_polling_enabled defaults to false in test, so `execute` short-circuits and both pass even if those guards were deleted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:32 — The "valid host" examples stub both `perform_retrieve` and `retrieved_recently?` on the object under test, verifying only the two-line boolean wiring in `retrieve`; nothing real is exercised.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:44 — TopicEmbed.import_remote` (the only path used by TopicRetriever and the rewritten disqus.thor) has no test whatsoever, including its nil-title/readability behaviour.

adjudication.rationale: It’s true that the diff adds `TopicEmbed.import_remote` and there is no direct spec exercising it (the new `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` only covers `.import`, and the new TopicRetriever spec stubs behavior without actually calling `.import_remote`). adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:43 — The spec asserts `TopicRetriever.new` is called, but the controller enqueues Jobs::RetrieveTopic; the mock takes no `.with(...)` so embed_url and user_id are never verified and the job layer is skipped.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:8 — "is 404 without an embed_url" never reaches `params.require`: blank embeddable_host makes ensure_embeddable reject first, so it duplicates the missing-host case instead of testing the required param.

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, the before_filter `ensure_embeddable` runs before `embed_url = params.require(:embed_url)`. `ensure_embeddable` raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` if `SiteSetting.embeddable_host.blank?`. The default in `config/site_settings.yml` sets `embeddable_host: ''` (blank), and the spec `it "is 404 without an embed_url"` does not stub `embeddable_host` or `request.referer`. Therefore the request will be rejected by `ensure_embeddable` before `params.require(:embed_url)` is evaluated, so the spec does not actually test the missing `embed_url` parameter behavior and effectively overlaps with the missing-host rejection case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — No example covers a referer whose host differs from embeddable_host, nor the `rescue URI::InvalidURIError` branch for a malformed Referer header.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` rejects requests when `URI(request.referer).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and also rescues `URI::InvalidURIError`. The added spec `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` covers (1) missing `embed_url`, (2) missing `embeddable_host`, and (3) "no referer"; it does not include any example where the referer is present but has a different host than `embeddable_host`, nor an example where `request.referer` is a malformed URI that triggers the `rescue URI::InvalidURIError` branch. So the finding about missing test coverage for those branches is accurate and verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_revisor.rb:85 — @post.save` became `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, changing validation behaviour for every revision, with no post_revisor spec added or updated.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `PostRevisor#update_post` from always validating on save to conditionally skipping validations only when `@opts[:skip_validations]` is passed. This is explicitly exercised by new code in `TopicEmbed.import` which calls `revisor.revise!(..., skip_validations: true, ...)`, implying the previous behavior (always validating) was incompatible with the new embed/import flow. The finding’s complaint that this is a problem “for every revision” is overstated (it’s opt-in via an option), and “no spec added/updated” is not itself a verifiable defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:130 — Post#cook` now returns raw for `raw_html` posts, bypassing the whole cooking/sanitization pipeline, with no post_spec coverage — only an indirect assertion inside topic_embed_spec.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which explicitly bypasses the normal cooking pipeline (including any sanitization/normalization that happens inside `post_analyzer.cook`). The new embed/import paths set `cook_method: :raw_html` (e.g., `TopicEmbed.import` via `PostCreator`), and RSS polling imports `i.content` after `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` without any additional sanitization before saving. The embed view then renders `raw post.cooked`, so for `raw_html` posts this becomes `raw post.raw`, creating a verifiable XSS risk if feed/remote content contains unsafe HTML. Test coverage is indeed only indirect (topic_embed_spec asserts `post.cooked == post.raw`), with no dedicated `post_spec` for this behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:39 — The update example only greps `cooked`; it never asserts content_sha1 was updated, that no second topic/embed row was created, or the unchanged-sha1 no-op path.

adjudication.rationale: The cited line is in a newly added spec. The finding is about insufficient test assertions/coverage (it doesn’t check content_sha1 update, duplicate rows, or the no-op path), but that is not a verifiable defect in the production code introduced by the diff. The test as written is valid and will pass/fail based on `post.cooked`, so the issue is an optional improvement rather than a real bug/security/correctness problem in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:56 — absolutize_urls is tested only with a plain http root-relative link; https, non-default ports, nil/empty href-src, and protocol-relative `//host/x` (whose leading slashes get stripped) are uncovered.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` and a spec that covers one root-relative `href` and `src` case. It is true that the spec does not exercise https URLs, non-default ports, or protocol-relative URLs (`//host/x`). However, the proposed finding is primarily about missing test coverage, not a defect introduced by the code. Additionally, some listed cases aren’t problematic in the implementation: `nil/empty` `href`/`src` are explicitly guarded with `present?`, and https/non-default ports are already handled via `uri.scheme`, `uri.host`, and conditional `uri.port` inclusion. While protocol-relative URLs would indeed be incorrectly rewritten by the current logic (because they start with `/`), the finding doesn’t actually claim the behavior is wrong—only that it’s “uncovered” by tests—so it doesn’t clearly identify a real defect in the diff as written.
